skill.name: nextjs-devtools
skill.description: Inspect and debug Next.js applications through an MCP client. Use it to list routes, inspect components, review build metadata, and query configuration.
skill.summary: MCP-based Next.js inspection for routes, components, build data, and configuration.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most markdown backtick and system-reconnaissance alerts are false positives from documentation formatting or MCP request identifiers. The real risks are shell-based stdio process launch, HTTP MCP connectivity, and unpinned npx package execution. No prompt-injection language was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Stdio transport runs a command string through shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Parse the stdio command into an argument list, disable shell=True, and allow only reviewed MCP server commands.
Pin an exact package version and document package provenance before recommending automated execution.

remediation.issue: HTTP transport can send MCP requests and headers to configured URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Default to localhost, warn before remote URLs, and avoid passing secrets in headers or parameters.

remediation.issue: Skill documentation encourages command execution without an explicit safety note.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear confirmation step before commands that start processes or install npm packages.

semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users and agents to run npx next-devtools-mcp@latest, and the start script launches the same unpinned package. This creates supply-chain risk because future package versions can change without review.

content.user_title: Inspect Next.js Apps with MCP DevTools
content.value_statement: Next.js projects can hide route, component, and build details across many files. This skill queries Next.js DevTools through MCP and summarizes that information.
actual_capabilities: Lists routes exposed by a Next.js DevTools MCP server.
Retrieves details for a specific route when a route parameter is provided.
Lists React components reported by the MCP server.
Reads build information from the connected Next.js tooling.
Queries Next.js configuration through the MCP server.
Connects to MCP servers over HTTP or stdio transports.
limitations: It is intended for Next.js projects only.
It requires a compatible Next.js DevTools MCP server.
It may run external commands when stdio transport is used.
It reports inspection data but does not directly fix application code.

use_cases.title: Audit Route Coverage
use_cases.description: List app routes and inspect a specific route before changing navigation.

use_cases.title: Debug Build Configuration
use_cases.description: Compare reported build settings with expected Next.js project configuration.

use_cases.title: Map Component Structure
use_cases.description: Review component discovery output during onboarding or refactoring.

prompt_templates.title: List Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nextjs-devtools to list all routes for this Next.js project. Summarize dynamic routes and API routes separately.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nextjs-devtools to inspect the route /api/auth. Explain its parameters, metadata, and related files.

prompt_templates.title: Review Build Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nextjs-devtools to get build information and configuration. Identify settings that could affect deployment or caching.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Check App Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nextjs-devtools to list routes, components, build info, and config. Produce a concise risk review before a migration.

output_examples.output: A grouped route summary with page routes, API routes, and dynamic route notes.

output_examples.input: Why is my production build different from development?
output_examples.output: A build-focused checklist that highlights Next.js settings, configuration differences, and follow-up checks.

output_examples.input: Show components used in the app.
output_examples.output: A component inventory summary with names and likely locations from the MCP server output.

best_practices: Run the tool from the Next.js project root so discovery uses the right context.
Pin and review the MCP server package before automated command execution.
Use local MCP URLs unless you explicitly trust the remote server and headers.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for non-Next.js React projects.
Do not pass secrets in headers or tool parameters unless the MCP server is trusted.
Do not rely on @latest package execution in production automation.

faq.question: Does this edit my application?
faq.answer: No. The documented tools inspect routes, components, build info, and config. Any changes must be made separately.

faq.question: Do I need a running MCP server?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the start script or a compatible HTTP or stdio MCP server.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: Use confirmation. The bundled client can run external commands and make HTTP requests.

faq.question: What projects are supported?
faq.answer: It is intended for Next.js apps, not general React or non-Next.js projects.

faq.question: Why are routes missing?
faq.answer: Run from the project root and confirm the Next.js DevTools MCP server can inspect the app.
